glosses: to talk or speak unnecessarily lengthily; to talk idly; to engage in unsubstantiated talk; to babble

examples.text: Als guter Politiker hat unser Bürgermeister auf der Bühne so lange gelabert, dass die Verspätung des Orchesters gar nicht auffiel.
examples.translation: Being a good politician, our mayor extended his speech on stage so much that the delayed appearance of the orchestra went unnoticed.
examples.english: Being a good politician, our mayor extended his speech on stage so much that the delayed appearance of the orchestra went unnoticed.

examples.text: Wenn der Peter mal gute Laune hat, hört er den ganzen Abend nicht auf zu labern.
examples.translation: When Peter is in a good mood for once, he won’t stop babbling for the rest of the night.
examples.english: When Peter is in a good mood for once, he won’t stop babbling for the rest of the night.

glosses: to chat; to talk among each other (usually about light topics); the verb retains a certain nuance, but becomes rather neutral

examples.text: Und? Was habt ihr gemacht? — Och, nur Kaffee getrunken und schön mal gelabert.
examples.translation: So? What did you guys do? — Oh, we just drank coffee and had a nice chat.
examples.english: So? What did you guys do? — Oh, we just drank coffee and had a nice chat.

examples.text: Sie labert oft dummes Zeug.

glosses: Dégoiser, tenir de grands discours, souvent creux.

examples.text: Der Minister hat lange gelabert.
examples.translation: Le ministre a longtemps tenu le crachoir.

glosses: Tchatcher, parler, bavarder de manière décontractée.

examples.text: Ich habe zufällig eine alte Freundin getroffen und mit ihr dann gleich über eine Stunde gelabert.
examples.translation: J’ai rencontré par hasard une vieille amie et tchatché avec elle plus d’une heure.

examples.text: Die beiden laberten jeden Tag über die Nachbarn.
examples.translation: Ces deux-là comméraient tous les jours sur les voisins.

glosses: ohne Substanz und/oder unnötig lange, gewunden und umständlich, wortreich reden oder monologisieren

examples.text: Unser Bürgermeister hat als guter Politiker, der er ist, auf der Bühne länger gelabert; so fiel die Verspätung des Orchesters nicht auf.
‚Ach, laber nicht!‘ (Entgegnung auf Substanzloses)
‚Laber hier nicht rum!‘

glosses: ungezwungen miteinander reden, sich entspannt unterhalten

examples.text: ‚Laber hier nicht rum!‘
Ich habe zufällig eine alte Freundin beim Einkaufen getroffen und mit ihr dann gleich über eine Stunde gelabert.

glosses: To talk rapidly without making much sense.

examples.text: “There you go blatherin’,” said Brindle, intending a mild rebuke.

It was at the unveiling of Sir John Gray's statue. Edmund Dwyer Gray was speaking, blathering away, and here was this old fellow, crabbed-looking old chap, looking at him from under his bushy eyebrows.
On and on he blathered, taking refuge in the one thing he felt lent him superiority: words.

glosses: To say (something foolish or nonsensical); to say (something) in a foolish or overly verbose way.

examples.text: Then, just before the wedding, the old man feels he’s honor bound to tell his future son-in-law the secret of his past; so the damned idiot blathers the whole story of his killing the man and breaking jail!
[…] the church attitude has never been that a teacher should be allowed to blather anything that comes into his head without any accountability at all.
That is the worst of being in an Irish regiment, nothing can be done widout ever so much blather;
Will you cease your blather of mutiny and treason and courts-martial?
With years of proofreading under my belt, I knew exactly the blather and bluster favoured by professional politicians.

1596, Charles Fitzgeoffrey, Sir Francis Drake His Honorable Lifes Commendation, and His Tragicall Deathes Lamentation, Oxford: Joseph Barnes,
[…] on Vlisses Circe did bestowe
A blather, where the windes imboweld were,

glosses: The high-pitched bark of a small dog, or similar.

examples.text: Had I taken his accusations seriously I might have recommended a change in my under-managership, but I never could translate our jammy products into gas or explosives or even poison. Still yap, at least as concerned Beldite's.
They couldn’t rise above their calls for peace. Those who weren’t “defenders of the fatherland” were incapable of anything except yap and blather about “stopping the war.”
Shut your yap!

glosses: A badly behaved person, especially a child.
Of a small dog, to bark.
To talk, especially excessively; to chatter.

examples.text: You’re always yapping, I wish you’d shut up.
Ante up! Yap that fool!

glosses: dat wat niet waar of redelijk is

examples.text: Wat een onzin is dat, zeg!.
Heb ik echt nooit iets geweten? Wat een onzin om te denken dat je na veertien jaar huwelijk elke dagelijkse stap van de ander kent.
Arend had gemopperd dat het onzin was dat hij mee moest, zoiets kon ik prima alleen; hij wilde een hard matras, zoals we altijd hadden gehad.

glosses: Hablar varias personas recíprocamente durante algún tiempo.

examples.text: —En las noches de luna, cuando su plateada luz resbalaba sobre la cima de los montes, ¿te acuerdas cómo charlábamos en voz baja entre las diáfanas sombras?

glosses: En particular, charlar₁ mucho pero con poco contenido.

examples.text: Si los indios lo(s) parecen, es por falta de encadenación de asuntos, y así, cuando van a una diligencia de cuidado, es preciso examinarlos por puntos muy menudos, si se pretende saber algo. Ni se piense que es porque no entienden el castellano, pues lo mismo les sucede en su idioma, como he observado, que lo que ellos charlan en un cuarto de hora lo traduce el intérprete en un minuto.
Yo iba á responderle; pero como el Conde conoce la viveza de mi genio, me hizo señas de callarme, de modo que no encontrando Su Reverencia opositores, seguia charlando mas que catorce.

glosses: Revelar por indiscreción algo que no debía decirse.
